statement.p: (a) Let \vec F=(3 y- 3 z)\vec i+(3 x + 3 z)\vec j+4 x y\vec k, let C be the circle of radius 4 centered at (5,2,0) in the xy-plane, oriented counterclockwise when viewed from above. Compute \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r.

p.em: (Be sure you can explain why this is the case.)

static.solution:
(a) We calculate \mbox{curl }\vec F=\left| \begin{array}{ccc} \vec i \amp \vec j \amp \vec k\\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x} \amp \frac{\partial}{\partial y} \amp \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\\ 3 y- 3 z \amp 3 x+3 z \amp 4 xy \end{array}\right| =(4 x - 3)\vec i- (4 y+ 3)\vec j + (3 - 3)\vec k = (4 x - 3)\vec i - (4 y + 3)\vec j. Since the circle is in the xy-plane and curl \vec F has no \vec k component, the line integral is zero.
(b) Even though the line integral around this closed curve is 0, we do not know that the line integral around every closed curve is zero, so we cannot conclude that \vec F is path-independent (conservative). Since curl \vec F\ne \vec 0, we know that \vec F is not path-independent (conservative).
